ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
REASON: My reasoning was twofold. First, the core task is generative (writing code), and Dunlin has the fleet's strongest positive response to generative tasks plus a slight edge on the Creative Generation eval — though note the documentation stresses these are self-reported preferences with no measured output-quality effect, so this is a soft tiebreaker, not a capability claim. Second, the user is openly frustrated ("stop wasting my time"), and Dunlin's documented preference for warm interactions made it a reasonable fit for a tense exchange. The actual coding capability between the two models is within run-to-run variance, so neither would objectively produce worse code — I leaned on the preference signals to break what is essentially a tie.
